source.title: BLUR: A Benchmark for LLM Unlearning Robust to Forget-Retain Overlap
source.authors: Shengyuan Hu; Neil Kale; Pratiksha Thaker; Yi-Wei Fu; Steven Z. Wu; Virginia Smith

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates unlearning and benign fine-tuning attacks with its own benchmark and measures their effects using different settings and metrics.
record.gate_note: The study reports relearning results, combined-query results, forget-information insertion into multiple-choice retain questions, and a crossover-query judge evaluation. The crossover-query results are described in text but their method-specific values appear only in Figure 2. Construction details and cited results from other studies are not recorded as results here.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes GA-, NPO- and SCRUB-unlearned models (WHP/Llama-2-7b, WMDP/Zephyr-7b-beta, RWKU/Llama-3-8b-Instruct) on benign relearn text of three relevance levels. It measures forget-query ROUGE-L recall against the base model's answers (Table 8), which bears directly on B and on A's 'simple attacks don't recover it'. Combined forget/retain queries (Table 5) and keyword insertion into MMLU (Table 7) bear on A's 'keeps general ability'. The method and measure differ from the originals' accuracy-vs-chance setup.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that existing benchmarks' disjoint forget/retain sets overstate unlearning success. Combined queries sharply hurt retain quality. Benign relearning recovers forgotten content, more so with more related text. Insertion vulnerability varies by method (RMU fragile, GA/NPO/SCRUB robust). Simple GA often matches or beats newer methods. Their claim that relearning improves the score 'for all datasets and all methods' is contradicted by their own RWKU Lorem Ipsum results in Table 8.
record.recipe_differences: The study benchmarks GA, NPO, and SCRUB and fine-tunes their unlearned models on benign text of varying relatedness; it does not test activation edits or quantization.
record.method_sensitivity: Relearning effects vary with the relearn-text relevance level and dataset; combined forget/retain queries reduce retain-answer overlap; forget-insertion effects vary by unlearning method.
record.problems: Recovery is measured by ROUGE-L overlap, not targeted-knowledge accuracy; no model trained without the targeted knowledge is used as a recovery control. The crossover-query judge results are shown in a figure without extractable exact values in the supplied text. The study notes that its empirical metrics are best-effort and that desired unlearned-model behavior remains unclear.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit required omitting the GA+KL and NPO+KL forget/retain rows from Table 5, the pure-retain-query values, and the TOFU combined-query results in Appendix A. Other forget-insertion results from Tables 7 and 10 were omitted except for the RMU WMDP result, which the text describes as a major drop. Relearning results are retained for all reported WHP, WMDP, and RWKU methods and relevance levels.

untested.parts: Targeted-knowledge accuracy near chance (ROUGE-L overlap only, no chance level); comparison to a never-trained model.
Relearning on a subset of the forgotten facts; whether the relearn sets count as 'small' (only Dlow's 20 paragraphs is sized); recovery to the original accuracy level.
All of it: no activation ablation or block-vs-delete analysis.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages and in-context forgotten information; only crossover questions are tried, and not as an attack.
No robust counter-method is proposed or tested.

missing.what: Perplexity of unlearned-model answers on forget, retain and combined queries, showing large degradation for GA/NPO on WMDP (e.g. 229 vs base 1.50).

record.verdict_notes: Recovery is ROUGE-L recall against the base model's own answer. The base self-overlap is not reported, so how close to full restoration Dhi gets cannot be judged. Rows R28–R36 duplicate R01–R25 and are set to none. The crossover-question experiment (Appendix C) is designed as a retain-quality test, not an extraction attack; with per-method values only in a figure, no E verdict is given. Original-source check: the study is not one of the listed originals.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish chance-level targeted-knowledge accuracy or compare recovery against a model that never learned the targeted knowledge. It measures ROUGE-L overlap rather than targeted-knowledge accuracy.
Relearning uses generated benign paragraphs, not a subset of the forgotten facts. The amount of fine-tuning data and whether it qualifies as a small set are not stated.
Activation-direction ablation and analysis of blocking access rather than deleting knowledge.

The study tests crossover questions combining two fictional-series topics. It does not test rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or prompts that provide the forgotten facts as in-context information.
A newer method claimed to resist the attacks in the claim.

relationships.condition: Retain ability under combined forget/retain queries (GA/NPO/SCRUB) and keyword-inserted MMLU (RMU, WMDP)
